message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: client build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/client-build.yml'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'biome.json'
      - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
      - 'apps/public-viewer/**'
      - 'apps/shared/**'
      - 'packages/report-schema/**'
      - 'utils/dummy-server/**'
      - '!apps/public-viewer/**/*.md'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/client-build.yml'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'biome.json'
      - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
      - 'apps/public-viewer/**'
      - 'apps/shared/**'
      - 'packages/report-schema/**'
      - 'utils/dummy-server/**'
      - '!apps/public-viewer/**/*.md'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 7

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 9.15.4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: './pnpm-lock.yaml'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Biome の lint / format を強制する。ローカルでは `pnpm run format` で直せる
      - name: Run Biome check
        run: pnpm exec biome ci --reporter=github apps/public-viewer utils/dummy-server

      - name: Run API-less dynamic build
        run: pnpm --filter @kouchou-ai/public-viewer build

      - name: Start static export fixture API
        run: |
          node <<'NODE' &
          const http = require("node:http");
          const fs = require("node:fs");
          const path = require("node:path");

          const root = process.cwd();
          const report = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, "utils/dummy-server/app/reports/example/hierarchical_result.json"), "utf8");
          const meta = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, "utils/dummy-server/public/meta/metadata.json"), "utf8");
          const reports = JSON.stringify([
            {
              slug: "example",
              status: "ready",
              title: "[テスト]人類が人工知能を開発・展開する上で、最優先すべき課題は何でしょうか？",
              description: "static export fixture",
              isPubcom: true,
              visibility: "public",
            },
          ]);

          http
            .createServer((request, response) => {
              response.setHeader("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*");
              response.setHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");

              if (request.url === "/meta/metadata.json") {
                response.end(meta);
                return;
              }

              if (request.url === "/reports") {
                response.end(reports);
                return;
              }

              if (request.url === "/reports/example") {
                response.end(report);
                return;
              }

              response.statusCode = 404;
              response.end(JSON.stringify({ error: "not found" }));
            })
            .listen(8002, "127.0.0.1");
          NODE

          for _ in {1..20}; do
            if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8002/meta/metadata.json >/dev/null; then
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

          echo "static export fixture API did not start" >&2
          exit 1

      # shell ビルドはレポートに依存しない HTML を 1 枚だけ出力する。
      # 直後の static export と同じ fixture API が見えている状態で、
      # レポート由来のルート (example) が出ないことを確かめる。
      - name: Run shell build
        run: pnpm --filter @kouchou-ai/public-viewer build:shell
        env:
          API_BASEPATH: 'http://127.0.0.1:8002'
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASEPATH: 'http://127.0.0.1:8002'
          NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_API_KEY: 'xxxxxxxxxx'

      - name: Assert the shell output is independent of the reports
        run: |
          set -eu
          out="apps/public-viewer/out"
          test -f "$out/__shell__/index.html"
          if [ -e "$out/example" ]; then
            echo "shell ビルドがレポート由来のルートを出力しました: example" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          # ルートも shell も、fixture のレポートを HTML に焼き込んでいないこと
          for page in "$out/index.html" "$out/__shell__/index.html"; do
            if grep -q "人類が人工知能を開発・展開する上で" "$page"; then
              echo "shell ビルドがレポートの内容を焼き込みました: $page" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          rm -rf "$out"
        shell: bash

      - name: Run static export build
        run: pnpm --filter @kouchou-ai/public-viewer build:static
        env:
          API_BASEPATH: 'http://127.0.0.1:8002'
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASEPATH: 'http://127.0.0.1:8002'
          NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_API_KEY: 'xxxxxxxxxx'

      - name: Record the preview source commit
        run: |
          test -f apps/public-viewer/out/index.html
          test -f apps/public-viewer/out/example/index.html
          git rev-parse HEAD > apps/public-viewer/out/BUILD_COMMIT.txt

      - name: Upload static viewer preview
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: static-viewer-${{ github.sha }}
          path: apps/public-viewer/out/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Pull Docker base image with registry fallback
        id: base-image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          RETRY=3
          for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= RETRY; attempt++)); do
            registry=""
            if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then
              registry="public.ecr.aws/docker/library/"
            fi
            if docker pull --platform linux/amd64 "${registry}node:22-alpine"; then
              printf 'registry=%s\n' "$registry" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi

            if [ "$attempt" -lt "$RETRY" ]; then
              echo "Base image pull failed (attempt $attempt/$RETRY); retrying via ECR Public in $((attempt * 10)) seconds..." >&2
              sleep "$((attempt * 10))"
            fi
          done

          exit 1

      - name: Run Docker build
        env:
          BASE_IMAGE_REGISTRY: ${{ steps.base-image.outputs.registry }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            -f ./apps/public-viewer/Dockerfile \
            --build-arg REGISTRY="$BASE_IMAGE_REGISTRY" \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASEPATH=http://localhost:8000 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLIC_API_KEY=xxxxxxxxxx \
            --build-arg API_BASEPATH=http://api:8000 \
            -t kouchou-ai-public-viewer-ci .
",
  "rationale": "The workflow currently has no job-level timeout, leaving it vulnerable to runaway executions. Historical CI runs for this workflow show consistent completion within 3-5 minutes (max observed ~4.8 minutes). The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) demonstrates a 26.8% elapsed-time reduction by adding an explicit timeout-minutes bound to a similar single-job Node.js workflow. Adding timeout-minutes: 7 provides ~45% operational headroom above the observed maximum while still bounding pathological runs. This change preserves all build and test coverage, adds no new permissions or network access, and aligns with the pattern's safety guidance to choose an explicit budget with headroom and measure false timeout failures separately.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization.

The workflow is a client build workflow that:
1. Checks out code
2. Sets up pnpm and Node.js
3. Installs dependencies
4. Runs Biome check
5. Runs API-less dynamic build
6. Starts a static export fixture API
7. Runs shell build
8. Asserts shell output is independent of reports
9. Runs static export build
10. Records preview source commit
11. Uploads static viewer preview
12. Pulls Docker base image with registry fallback
13. Runs Docker build

Looking at the evidence, I see several patterns:
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Adding timeout-minutes to jobs (experiment shows 26.8% elapsed savings)
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Setting fail-fast: true for matrix jobs (but this workflow doesn't use matrix)
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Caching dependencies (already using cache: 'pnpm' in setup-node)
- P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs (could be applicable for push/pull_request)

The workflow currently has no timeout-minutes set on the job. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern has experimental evidence showing 26.8% elapsed savings (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508). The pattern suggests adding a custom timeout to bound jobs.

Looking at the workflow, it's a single job (not a matrix), so fail-fast doesn't apply. The workflow already uses pnpm cache via setup-node.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern seems applicable here. The experiment shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a similar job reduced elapsed time by ~27%. The workflow runs on ubuntu-latest and does various builds and Docker operations. A 5-minute timeout seems reasonable given the historical runs show completion in ~4 minutes (looking at the CI history: runs take about 3-4 minutes).

Let me check the CI history:
- Run 45538598123: 3:14:34 to 3:18:16 = ~3.7 minutes
- Run 45534897320: 2:42:45 to 2:46:06 = ~3.3 minutes
- Run 45530983209: 2:10:02 to 2:14:45 = ~4.7 minutes
- Run 45530963472: 2:09:53 to 2:13:50 = ~3.9 minutes
- Run 45530955444: 2:09:49 to 2:14:40 = ~4.8 minutes

So runs typically take 3-5 minutes. A 5-minute timeout would be tight but reasonable with some headroom. The pattern suggests "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom" and "Measure false timeout failures separately". Given the max observed is ~4.8 minutes, 5 minutes might be too tight. Maybe 6-7 minutes would be safer.

However, the experiment used 5 minutes and showed success. The pattern's preconditions include "Representative successful-duration history exists" which we have.

Let me also consider P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE for canceling superseded runs. This workflow triggers on push and pull_request to main. For push events, if multiple pushes happen quickly, canceling the previous run could save resources. The pattern has estimated benefits (1.9% free, 4.1% paid VM time reduction).

But the workflow doesn't have concurrency settings. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress would be a valid optimization.

Let me check if there are any contraindications for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: "Release or deployment work" and "Distinct branches share a cancellation group". This is a build workflow, not deployment, and it only runs on main branch for push, so distinct branches aren't an issue (PRs are also on main branch).

Actually, looking at the triggers:
- push: branches: [main]
- pull_request: branches: [main]

So both push and PR target main. If we add concurrency, we'd want to cancel superseded runs for the same branch/PR. The pattern suggests "Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR".

Given the evidence, I think both P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE could apply. But the instruction says to propose "any evidence-supported CI optimization" and choose APPLY for a supported change. I should pick the one with the strongest evidence.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has experimental evidence (measured_ci_workflow_on_fork) showing 26.8% savings. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE has simulation estimates.

Also, the experiment for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows a very similar workflow structure (single job, ubuntu-latest, Node.js setup, npm ci, lint, typecheck, etc.).

I'll go with P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and add a timeout-minutes to the job. Based on the history, I'll use 7 minutes to provide more headroom than the experimental 5 minutes (since our max observed is ~4.8 minutes, 7 gives ~45% headroom).

Wait, the experiment used 5 minutes and the baseline median was 41 seconds, optimized 30 seconds. That's a very short job. Our job takes 3-5 minutes. The timeout should be based on our history, not the experiment's.

The pattern says: "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom" and "Measure false timeout failures separately". With max observed ~4.8 minutes, a 7-minute timeout gives reasonable headroom.

Let me also check if the workflow already has any timeout - it doesn't.

So the change would be adding `timeout-minutes: 7` to the build job.

I'll also consider adding concurrency for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, but that's a separate pattern. The instruction says "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization" - singular. I'll pick the one with direct experimental evidence.

Decision: APPLY with P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, adding timeout-minutes: 7 to the build job.

Evidence IDs: experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT experiment) and pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (the pattern definition).

Let me construct the updated workflow.
